title: The Israeli-Palestinian Conflict
rootClaim: A sustainable peace in the Israeli-Palestinian conflict requires an immediate end to occupation, full recognition of Palestinian self-determination, and a viable two-state framework based on international law.

branches.text: Palestinian Right to Self-Determination & International Law: Decades of military occupation, settlement expansion, and blockade violate UN resolutions and human rights conventions.

children.text: West Bank Settlement Expansion: Illegal settlements fracture contiguous territorial sovereignty necessary for a viable independent Palestinian state.
Security Deterrence Defense: Demilitarized territorial buffer zones and intelligence control in the West Bank are vital for preventing existential attacks on Israeli population centers.
Disproportionality & Collective Punishment: Enforcing control through blockades, home demolitions, and arbitrary detention causes widespread civilian suffering violating Fourth Geneva Convention.

Non-State Military Encampment: Asymmetric combat in dense urban areas where militant groups operate near civilian infrastructure creates extreme operational complexity under international humanitarian law.
Right of Return (UN Resolution 194): Palestinian refugees displaced during the 1948 Nakba hold moral and legal claims to return to their ancestral homes.

branches.text: Israeli National Sovereignty & Existential Security: Israel possesses an inherent right to self-defense as a Jewish democratic state surrounded by hostile non-state proxies committed to its destruction.

children.text: Historical Indigenous Claim & Refuge: The Jewish people maintain continuous historical ties to the land and require a sovereign sanctuary against millennia of global antisemitism.
Demographic & Pluralist Challenge: Maintaining a Jewish majority while exercising control over millions of non-voting Palestinians threatens the state's democratic legitimacy.
Refusal of Past Peace Offers: Historic rejections of two-state compromise proposals by leadership in 1947, 2000 (Camp David), and 2008 demonstrate a lack of a partner for peace.

definitions.description: A proposed framework for resolving the conflict by establishing an independent Palestinian state alongside the sovereign state of Israel.
An international treaty defining humanitarian protections for civilians in war zones and occupied territories.
The political and moral claim that Palestinian refugees and their descendants have a right to return to homes left during the 1948 and 1967 conflicts.
The nationalist movement supporting the establishment and protection of a Jewish state in their ancestral homeland.
